questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.topic: Net flux from a charge inside a closed surface
questions.learningObjective: state that the net electric flux through a closed surface is fixed by the charge it encloses
questions.stem: A small positive charge sits at the centre of a hollow sphere that carries no charge of its own. What electric flux passes through the surface of that sphere?

options.text: A value set by the enclosed charge alone, whatever the sphere's size or the charge's place in it
Zero, because every field line stops as soon as it reaches the inner surface of the sphere
options.misconception: treats field lines as ending on a surface, which leaves the enclosed charge unaccounted for

options.text: A value that grows steadily as the radius of the sphere is made larger
options.misconception: believes a larger sphere intercepts more of the flux, though every line crosses it once

options.text: Zero, because the sphere is a closed conductor with nothing at all inside it
options.misconception: confuses an uncharged conducting shell with a cavity that does contain a charge

questions.explanation: Gauss's law says the net flux out of a closed surface is the charge inside it divided by eps0, and that is the whole story: every line the charge sends out must cross the surface exactly once, so the count cannot depend on the sphere's size or on where in the sphere the charge is put. The lines do not stop at the surface, they cross it and carry on into the space beyond. The claim that they end there is what forces a zero flux, and a zero flux is exactly what the law forbids for a nonzero enclosed charge.
questions.hint: Count the lines leaving the charge. Every one of them has to cross the surface.

questions.topic: Why a charge outside a surface adds no net flux
questions.learningObjective: explain that a source outside a closed surface sends as much flux in as out
questions.stem: A pair of equal and opposite charges sits close together, well outside a closed surface drawn around empty space. What net electric flux passes through that surface?

options.text: Zero, because every field line entering the region bounded by the surface leaves it again
Positive, because the field of the nearer positive charge dominates that whole region
options.misconception: keeps only the nearer source and forgets that the far one is bent back the other way

options.text: Zero, but only because the two charges happen to be equal and opposite
options.misconception: credits the cancellation of the charges rather than the closed shape of the surface

options.text: The same flux the pair would produce if it were the pair that got enclosed
options.misconception: assumes the flux depends on the total charge of the system wherever that charge sits

questions.explanation: Lines of field from the positive charge enter the region bounded by the surface where they pass closest to it, and every one of them must eventually cross the surface again on the way out, because the surface is closed and the charge is outside it. The negative charge contributes lines running the other way, which swap the order in which the crossings happen without changing the total. Gauss's law settles it: the right-hand side is the charge enclosed, which here is nothing at all, so the flux is zero. That is true for any charge outside the surface, paired or not.
questions.hint: Trace the lines from the nearer charge. Do all of them cross the surface the same way?

questions.topic: Net flux from several enclosed charges
questions.learningObjective: calculate the net electric flux from the algebraic sum of the enclosed charges
questions.stem: A closed surface encloses a charge of +6.0e-9 C and a charge of -2.0e-9 C, and nothing else. What net electric flux passes through the surface, in newton metre squared per coulomb? Take eps0 = 8.85e-12 F/m and give the number only.

The surface size never appears, which is the point of the law. Back-substituting, 452 times 8.85e-12 recovers 4.0e-9 C exactly.

The electric flux through an open surface equals the enclosed charge multiplied by eps0
options.misconception: uses an open surface and inverts eps0, so the two sides carry different units

options.text: The field at a point times the area of a surface equals the total charge in the universe
options.misconception: multiplies field by area without the normal component and charges everything everywhere

options.text: The electric flux out of any closed surface equals the enclosed charge times the area
options.misconception: puts an area factor on the right-hand side, which no form of the law contains

questions.stem: A bar magnet is placed inside a closed box and a small compass is moved all over the outside of that box. What does the total magnetic flux out of the box add up to?

options.text: Zero, because no magnetic field line begins or ends anywhere in space
The flux leaving the magnet's north pole alone, since that is where lines start
options.misconception: credits a north pole with starting field lines, which no magnetic pole does

options.text: A positive amount, because more lines leave through the box than enter it
options.misconception: counts the outward crossings without noticing the inward ones that balance them

options.text: A negative amount, because the south pole's lines run from outside into the box
options.misconception: allows a net in-flux through a closed surface, which the magnetic law forbids

Nothing, since a field that grows weaker with distance may simply stop being drawn

questions.topic: Choosing a surface that makes the flux integral easy
questions.learningObjective: use cylindrical symmetry to show the field inside a long charged pipe is zero
questions.stem: A long cylindrical metal pipe of great length is given a uniform charge per unit length. Which statement about the electric field in the empty bore of that pipe is correct?

options.text: It is zero, because on a coaxial cylinder the end caps cancel and the curved side carries no flux
It is zero, because a cylinder drawn inside the pipe encloses no charge at all
options.misconception: stops at the enclosed-charge count without using the end caps, which is not enough alone

options.text: It is zero, because the charge on the metal spreads itself evenly around the bore
options.misconception: reaches the right answer by an argument that would wrongly zero the field outside

options.text: It is not zero, and equals the charge per unit length over the bore circumference
options.misconception: borrows the result for the outside of the pipe and invents a charge inside the bore

The field is along the axis, so on each end cap it lies in the plane of the cap and the flux there is zero, and the curved side encloses no charge, so its flux is zero too. Symmetry says the field has the same value all round that curved surface, so a zero flux there means the field is zero there, and therefore zero throughout the bore. Note that the bare count of enclosed charge is not enough: a zero total flux is compatible with a field that goes out through one part and back through another, and the end caps are what rule that out.

questions.topic: Field of a uniformly charged infinite sheet
questions.learningObjective: calculate the field of a uniformly charged sheet from a pillbox

questions.topic: Displacement current between the plates of a charging capacitor
questions.learningObjective: state that a changing electric field between the plates behaves as a current
questions.stem: A parallel-plate capacitor is being charged through long wires, and nothing conductive joins the two plates. The wires plainly carry a current. What produces the magnetic field in the gap?

options.text: The rate at which the electric field in the gap is growing, which acts like a current
Nothing does, because the gap is an insulator and blocks any passage of charge
options.misconception: treats an insulating gap as blocking something that is a change of field, not a flow of charge

options.text: Conduction current crossing the gap from one plate to the other and back again
options.misconception: invents charge flowing across an insulator, which would simply short the capacitor out

options.text: The plates radiating while their charge is being rearranged on the surfaces
options.misconception: credits radiation for a field that stays confined during a slow charge

questions.explanation: The conduction current in the wire is just the rate at which charge piles onto the plates, and the same rate of change appears in the gap as a growing electric field. Maxwell's addition of a displacement current, eps0 multiplied by the rate of change of the field, carries that rate into the gap so that the magnetic field circling the wire continues smoothly through the capacitor and reappears on the far side. No charge crosses the gap at any point, which is why the term is called a displacement current rather than a real one, and why removing it makes the field discontinuous exactly where the charge is being stored.
questions.hint: Ask what is changing in the gap. A changing electric field acts like a current to the magnetic law.

options.text: 8.28e-9 T, from a circular path of radius 0.050 m enclosing the whole charging current
0 T, because no conduction current at all crosses the gap between the plates
options.misconception: omits the displacement current and so finds no field where one must exist

options.text: 4.14e-9 T, from halving the current because the two plates face each other
options.misconception: splits the current between two plates as though both of them were sources

options.text: 1.66e-8 T, from doubling the current to allow for the wire running back
options.misconception: adds the return wire into the enclosed current of a loop that excludes it

questions.learningObjective: explain the inconsistency that forced the displacement current term into the law
questions.stem: A circular loop is drawn round a charging capacitor so that one part of it runs down the wire and another part runs across the gap. What does the original Ampere law report as the enclosed current, and why is that wrong?

options.text: It reports the full charging current, which is right, because the current really is continuous
options.misconception: assumes conduction current is continuous everywhere, which is what the law cannot deliver

options.text: It reports the charging current in the wire, which is wrong because nothing crosses the gap
It reports no current at all, which is wrong because the wire plainly carries the current
options.misconception: reads the law as seeing only the dielectric part of the loop and so reporting zero

options.text: It reports the charging current divided by the plate area, which has the wrong units
options.misconception: expects a surface current density where the law asks for a total enclosed current

options.text: The flux of B through a surface equals mu_0 times the current it encloses

questions.learningObjective: identify the two equations of the set that express conservation of charge

The magnetic one says there are no magnetic monopoles anywhere

Along the wire, in the same direction as the conventional current that flows
options.misconception: supposes the energy rides down the wire with the current instead of across the fields

options.text: Out of the wire, along its surface and away from the resistance that is dissipating
options.misconception: reverses the cross product, so power appears to be radiated away from the wire

questions.topic: How power reaches a resistor through empty space
questions.learningObjective: explain that the fields, not the moving charge, deliver power to a resistance
questions.stem: A textbook shows a battery driving current through a resistor and says the battery supplies the power, although no energy is carried along the wire by the moving charge. Explain in your own words how the power actually reaches the resistor.

answer.exemplar: The current is the same everywhere round the loop, so the charge drifting along the wire is not being consumed and is not ferrying the energy anywhere. The energy is in the fields, and the fields are all around the wire rather than inside it. Along the outgoing wire the electric field points towards the resistor and the magnetic field circles the wire, so the cross product of the two, the energy flow vector, points radially inward: power flows out of the surrounding space into the metal along the length of the resistance. Where the wire runs back towards the battery the potential falls the other way, the electric field reverses, the cross product reverses with it, and power leaves the metal again, travelling back to the source through the space on that side. So the return leg is an emitter of power into its surroundings rather than a passive one, and nothing has to be piped down either conductor for any of this to happen, which is exactly why a resistance behaves as a region of space that soaks up radiation-power. Close a surface around the resistor and the net flux into it equals the power it turns into heat, 8.0 W in the case quoted; close one around the battery and an equal flux goes the other way. The battery's only job is to hold the two ends of the loop at different potentials, and everything else is done by the fields in between.

questions.explanation: The energy flow vector points into the resistance and outward again along the return wire, so power crosses the space surrounding the conductors rather than travelling inside them. Closing a surface round the resistor shows the net inward flux equals the heat it produces.
questions.hint: Ask which way the cross product of the two fields points along each leg of the loop in turn.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.topic: Why the displacement current had to be added
questions.learningObjective: explain what a charging capacitor exposed and how the correction restored the law
questions.stem: Before the correction, the law relating the circulation of a magnetic field to the current around it worked for every steady circuit. Explain in your own words what a charging capacitor exposed, and what fixed it.

answer.exemplar: The original law says that the work done by the magnetic field in going once round a closed loop is fixed by the current passing through the loop. That works for a steady circuit because no current ever leaves the wire, so every surface that can be stretched across the loop cuts the same current however it is drawn. A charging capacitor breaks precisely that assumption. Take a loop that runs down the wire into one plate, across the space between the plates, and back along the other wire. Close the spanning surface through the wire and the enclosed current is the full charging current; close it through the gap instead and the enclosed current is zero, because no charge crosses an insulating space. One loop, two different answers, and any law whose value depends on how you chose the surface is not a law at all. The repair starts from noticing that what crosses the gap is not charge but a change of field. While charge piles onto a plate, the electric field between the plates grows, and that growth is itself a current-like quantity, eps0 multiplied by the rate of change of the field, whose size in the gap is exactly the current arriving by wire. Adding it to the conduction current makes the enclosed total identical for both surfaces, the field runs smoothly through the capacitor, and the law gives the same answer however the surface is drawn. The correction also handed over a bonus: with the electric and magnetic laws in this form, the speed at which the coupled changes travel works out as one over the square root of eps0 mu_0, and inserting the measured values of those two constants returns the speed of light. Neither law had ever mentioned light, so this was not a designed result but a consistency that had been waiting to be noticed.

questions.explanation: A loop closed through the wire and a loop closed through the gap gave different enclosed currents, which made the law depend on the surface chosen. The growing electric field in the gap supplies exactly the current that was missing.
questions.hint: Ask what a surface spanning the loop can enclose in each of the two cases, and why the two answers differ.

questions.stem: The equations of classical electromagnetism were written down before relativity was understood, yet they already predict that an observer in motion sees a magnetic field where a stationary observer sees only an electric one. Explain how that came about.

answer.exemplar: The starting point is that those equations contain two constants, the permittivity and the permeability of empty space, and no third parameter of any kind. Combine them the only way that yields a speed, one over the square root of their product, and a number comes out that no parameter in the equations can influence. Nothing in that expression describes an emitter, a receiver, a medium or a clock, so the number has to be the same whoever is doing the measuring. But a speed that is the same in every frame is precisely the statement that the equations are unchanged under a change of frame, and invariance is a strong condition: once you require it, the fields cannot keep their separate identities, because a configuration that is purely electric in one frame has to remain a valid solution in the next, and the only way that can happen is for electric and magnetic fields to blend into one another. That is why a charge at rest in a laboratory is a source of magnetism to an observer travelling past it, and why the size of the magnetic field is fixed by the requirement that nothing the transformation produces can outrun the speed the constants set. In the numbers, the field of a charge moving at 0.60 of that speed alongside an electric field of 1.0e5 V per metre works out to 2.0e-4 T, and the companion calculation from the field of a moving point charge returns the same figure once the two constants are made consistent with one another. So relativity was not an extra postulate added to electromagnetism to make it fit. It was already latent in the one feature of the theory that could not be avoided, namely a fundamental speed built out of two measurable constants.

questions.explanation: The two constants in the field equations combine to fix a speed that no parameter can influence, so it must be frame-independent, and that invariance forces the electric and magnetic fields to mix under a change of frame.
questions.hint: Ask what the expression for the speed of the wave contains, and notice that it contains nothing about an observer.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.topic: Radiation pressure is ordinary momentum transfer
questions.learningObjective: show that radiation pressure follows from the definition of force
questions.stem: A student insists that radiation pressure is a special effect confined to light and cannot be reasoned about like any other push. Why is that not a defensible position?

options.text: It is ordinary momentum transfer, applied to something with no rest mass at all
It is a special effect, but it pushes surfaces with sound waves as well
options.misconception: calls it special while generalising it wrongly, since sound does not press this way

options.text: It applies to light alone, since a sound wave cannot push a surface at all
options.misconception: restricts the effect to light when the point is that it is not restricted

options.text: It is not a real force, only a way of describing how the surface warms up
options.misconception: denies the force, which a radiometer demonstrates directly

questions.explanation: Pressure is force per unit area, force is the rate of change of momentum, and the only unusual feature of radiation is that the momentum belongs to something with no rest mass. Apply those two definitions and the pressure follows without further argument, since it is just the momentum arriving each second per unit area. A beam of intensity 6.0e3 W per square metre arrives at 2.0e-5 Pa on an absorbing surface, and that is the arithmetic consequence of the definition rather than a property of light. What genuinely is special is not the push but the size of it, and the size is fixed by the momentum per unit of energy being one over the speed of light, which is what makes the effect small enough to need a clever instrument to see.
questions.hint: Start from the definition of pressure and follow it through the definition of force, ignoring what the thing is made of.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.topic: Reading a fast-particle survival table
questions.learningObjective: extract a mean life from a decay table and recognise the dilation factor in it
questions.stem: Muons with a rest-frame mean life of 2.2e-6 s arrive from the upper atmosphere at 0.998 of the speed of light. A ground array logs the fraction still undecayed against time on the ground clock: 0.750 at 1.0e-5 s, 0.563 at 2.0e-5 s, 0.422 at 3.0e-5 s, 0.317 at 4.0e-5 s, 0.238 at 5.0e-5 s. What mean life does the first row imply, and how does it compare with the rest-frame value?

options.text: About 3.5e-5 s, some sixteen times the rest-frame value of 2.2e-6 s
About 2.2e-6 s, unchanged, since the decay law is the same in every frame
options.misconception: applies the decay law without the frame change, the error this table exists to expose

options.text: About 3.5e-5 s, but a quarter of the rest value because the speed exceeds 0.99c
options.misconception: keeps the right number and reverses the direction of the effect into a reduction

options.text: About 2.2e-7 s, a tenth of the rest value, because the particles are moving so fast
options.misconception: divides by an arbitrary factor of ten and calls the result a contraction

questions.explanation: The decay law says the surviving fraction is the exponential of minus the time over the mean life, so 0.750 gives a mean life of minus 1.0e-5 over the natural logarithm of 0.750, and that logarithm is minus 0.2877, so 3.48e-5 s. Set against the rest-frame 2.2e-6 s the ratio is 15.8, which is the dilation factor at 0.998 of the speed of light, since the square root of 1 minus 0.996004 is 0.06321. The rows are internally consistent as well, each falling by a factor of 0.750 on the previous one. Reading the table classically, with 2.2e-6 s used directly, would predict only 0.011 surviving at 1.0e-5 s, some seventy times below what the array recorded, and that gap between prediction and measurement is the whole of the effect.
questions.hint: Invert the decay law using the first row, then divide by the rest-frame value to see the factor.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.topic: Why the classical and relativistic answers disagree for light
questions.learningObjective: explain that the classical addition rule assumes a rest mass
questions.stem: Adding the speed of a moving source to the speed of light gives a figure larger than the measured speed of light, yet light from a fast source is never measured arriving faster. Explain in your own words what that disagreement is telling you.

answer.exemplar: The addition that produces the impossible figure is a rule about ordinary objects. If a ball leaves the back of a moving train at walking speed, an observer on the platform adds the train's speed to it and measures something larger than he would have measured for the same throw made on the ground. That rule was built from ordinary experience, where every object has a rest mass and where speeds stay far below the speed of light, and it is a good rule inside those limits. It fails for light, and the important point is not that the rule has been misapplied but that its assumptions do not hold. Light has no rest mass, and something with no rest mass cannot be slowed down, added to, or caught up by anything. Ask what a source moving at 0.90 of the speed of light contributes to the speed of the light leaving it, and the honest answer taken from the field equations is nothing at all, because the speed of the wave is set by the two constants of empty space and nothing in that expression mentions an emitter. The striking part is the order in which this was discovered. Those equations were written down with no knowledge of relativity at all, and the same two constants that fix the speed of the wave also fix the limits on how the fields transform under a change of frame, so the theory had already ruled out any signal faster than that speed before anybody had measured light. So the measurement is not a correction to the classical rule. It is a sign that the classical rule was never entitled to be applied to something without a rest mass, and that the theory of the field had quietly said so all along.

questions.explanation: The addition rule assumes every object has a rest mass and that speeds stay far below that of light, and light satisfies neither assumption, so the rule was never entitled to be applied to it.
questions.hint: Ask what a moving source contributes to the speed of the light leaving it, and whether the expression for that speed mentions the source.
